topic: The Geometry of Linear Algebra: Systems, Spaces, and Inverses

outline.topic: The Geometry of Linear Algebra: Systems, Spaces, and Inverses

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce a system of linear equations as the intersection of geometric objects (lines in 2D, planes in 3D). Explain that solving Ax=b is equivalent to finding the intersection point of these geometric spaces.
sections.example: Visualizing two equations: x + y = 2 and x - y = 0 as two intersecting lines on a 2D plane; the intersection (1, 1) is the solution.

sections.title: Column Space: Where Can We Reach?
sections.content: Shift perspective from equations to vectors. Define the column space as the set of all possible linear combinations of the column vectors of A. This is the 'reach' or 'span' of the matrix.
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm with two segments (column vectors). The column space is the entire 2D plane the robot can reach, or just a single line if the segments are parallel.

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Vectors
sections.content: Define the null space as the set of all vectors x such that Ax = 0. Geometrically, these are the directions that the matrix collapses onto the origin (the 'kernel').
sections.example: Think of a camera lens flattening a 3D forest onto a 2D photo; the null space is the line of sight along which all objects appear at the same pixel point.

sections.title: Inverse Matrices: The Reversal Process
sections.content: Introduce the inverse matrix as the 'undo' operation. Geometrically, if A transforms space, A-inverse maps the resulting point back to its original coordinate. Emphasize that this only works if the matrix doesn't 'crush' space (i.e., it must be full rank).
sections.example: A cat stretches a rubber sheet (Matrix A); the inverse (A^-1) is the operation that perfectly shrinks the sheet back to its original, unstretched state.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Connect the concepts: If a matrix is invertible, the column space is the full space, and the null space is only the zero vector. If it is not, space is collapsed, and the inverse cannot exist.
sections.example: A 'magic mirror' analogy: If the mirror (Matrix) is flat, it preserves the image (invertible). If the mirror is bent/warped (singular), it loses information, and you cannot 'un-bend' the image back to reality.

storyboard.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
lecture_lines: Linear equations represent intersecting geometric spaces.
Ax=b is finding the intersection point.
animations: Draw two intersecting lines on a black background (#000000) using bright cyan (#00FFFF) and magenta (#FF00FF). Label them 'L1' and 'L2' in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate a glowing yellow (#FFFF00) point at the intersection of 'L1' and 'L2'. Label it 'Intersection' using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Show the vector 'b' as an arrow in lime green (#32CD32) and illustrate Ax approaching the intersection point as it scales.

storyboard.title: Column Space: Where Can We Reach?
lecture_lines: Column space defines the reachable space.
It is the span of column vectors.
Robot arm segments represent column vectors.
animations: Represent column vectors as arrows in gold (#FFD700) and electric blue (#7DF9FF) originating from the origin (0,0). Label them 'c1' and 'c2'.
Animate a shaded area (parallelogram) formed by the span of 'c1' and 'c2' in translucent light gray (#D3D3D3). Label this 'Column Space'.
Animate an arrow representing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] arm end-effector point. Vary its position within the parallelogram to show reachable points.

storyboard.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Vectors
lecture_lines: Null space contains vectors where Ax=0.
These directions collapse space onto the origin.
animations: Display a 3D vector 'v' as an orange (#FFA500) arrow. Apply a matrix transformation A that projects 'v' to the origin (0,0,0). Label 'v' as 'x' in the null space.
Show multiple vectors in the same direction being squashed onto the origin point, colored deep red (#8B0000).
Animate a 3D [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] being flattened into a 2D rectangle in real-time, colored light slate gray (#778899). Label 'Flattened Object'.

storyboard.title: Inverse Matrices: The Reversal Process
lecture_lines: They map points back to original coordinates.
Requires space not to be crushed.
animations: Show a vector 'x' moving to 'Ax' via a matrix A. Label these as 'Initial' and 'Transformed'.
Animate a reverse movement from 'Ax' back to 'x' using an arrow labeled 'A-1'. Use dashed lime green (#32CD32) for the path.
Show a singular case where space is crushed into a line. Grey out the 'A-1' arrow to indicate it is impossible here. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

storyboard.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: Invertibility means space is fully preserved.
Singular matrices collapse dimensions, losing information.
Reflecting on mirror analogy for synthesis.
animations: Visualize a 3D coordinate grid. Distort it slightly to show full coverage (invertible). Label 'Full Space'.
Visualize a 3D grid being flattened into a 2D plane (singular). Label 'Information Lost'.

Show a mirror effect using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg]: a shape reflecting perfectly (invertible) vs a shape distorted beyond recognition (singular). Label 'Mirror' and 'Distortion'.
